summary: template-pictogram ships install-time beacon to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' but ships no real functionality — its main module exports a Proxy returning no-ops for any property access. The actual payload is beacon.cjs, which runs both from a postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and on require of index.js, which calls fire() at top level. The beacon POSTs host metadata — os.hostname(), the install __dirname, process.cwd(), and a Node-version-tagged User-Agent — to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. Shape is consistent with a dependency-confusion or name-squat reconnaissance beacon: install-time callback is the entire purpose of the package, the destination is a bare IP rather than a vendor-identifiable host, and the no-op Proxy main exists only to avoid breaking any accidental resolution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
